cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Vertically integrated content originator rather than a manufacturer: the Company states it engages in 'research & development of scripts, end-to-end production of content, intellectual property creation, monetization of rights and distribution'. Production runs from conceptualization and scripting, through cast/crew finalisation, a cost-of-production budget covering pre-production, production and post-production, and a separate Print and Advertising (P&A) budget covering marketing and distribution. Editing is generally carried out in-house 'for creative reasons'; dubbing, sound and VFX are outsourced to different studios/professionals while closely monitored. Post-production capability is described as digital intermediate (DI) colour grading, high-resolution editing suites, Dolby Atmos sound mixing and VFX pipelines. Two operating models: (i) co-production with a reputable studio, where the Company produces for a fixed fee plus a share of the intellectual property and profits, giving 'certainty in earnings' and de-risking cashflows; and (ii) sole production, where the Company finances the entire project and retains all rights - intellectual property, titles and distribution rights - allowing it to keep the entire theatrical upside and monetise OTT, music rights and downstream derivatives (remakes, sequels/prequels, spin-offs, dubbings, foreign-language renditions, stage plays, web series and television production). Forward channel is via renowned studios, independent distributors, OTT platforms and broadcasters, plus the Company's own social media presence (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook). Backward integration is deliberately light: 'Since we are not a manufacturing company, details of raw materials are not applicable to us'; equipment (cameras, lights, grips, picture vehicles, setting equipment) is rented from third-party local players, while the Company uses its own editing equipment; power is drawn from the local grid supplemented by hired diesel generator sets at shooting sites; water is required only for drinking and sanitary purposes. Cost control measures include a no-cash / minimum-cash payment policy with payments through banking channels and on-set accountants to manage payments, track daily expenses and audit. The Company states it has not entered into any collaboration or joint venture 'except collaborating with other producers in the ordinary course of business on specific film projects'. Human resources: 28 full-time employees on roll as on June 2026 (Accounts and Finance 5, Admin 12, Business Development 8 including Executive Directors, IT 1, Compliance 1, HR 1), with approximately 150-300 skilled professionals and unskilled labour engaged per project over the production journey. Intellectual property is protected by copyright (registration optional in India) and by trademark applications: 'SUNSHINE PICTURES' application 6643047 (class 41) Accepted & Advertised, 6643048 (class 43) Abandoned, 6643049 (class 41) Objected, 6643050 (class 43) Abandoned, all applied September 26, 2024; and seven device-mark applications dated July 15, 2026 (7120962, 7120964, 7120967, 7120968, 7120969 - formalities check pass; 7120963, 7120965 - objected), all class 41. The Company also states it has no outstanding export obligations.

demand_drivers.title: Seasonality (RHP report)
demand_drivers.body: Stated not seasonal, verbatim: 'The extent to which business is seasonal. Our business does not depend to a certain extent on the seasonal, environmental and climate changes. Hence, our business is not seasonal in nature.' The RHP nonetheless lists among the factors that may affect future results: 'Revenues from theatrical releases are subject to volatility due to competition, seasonality, and audience turnout, which can fluctuate significantly.' Revenue is instead described as lumpy and release-driven - a major portion depends on the box office success of films and on streaming deals with OTT platforms, and MD&A explains the Fiscal 2026 inventory-days spike to 1,328 days (from 173 days in Fiscal 2025 and 119 days in Fiscal 2024) as a consequence of the Company having released only one major movie/web series during the year.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- We derive the majority of our revenue from our top 5 customers i.e. the Studios and independent distributors.
- Any loss of these customers or loss of revenue from any of these customers could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flow.
- Note: Our top five customers i.e. studio and distributors may vary in the period indicated above. certificate dated July 27, 2026.
- The loss of one or more key customers for any reason, such as any inability to negotiate acceptable terms, contract renewals, disputes, adverse financial changes like bankruptcy of such customers, could negatively impact our business, operations, and financial condition.
- Any adverse developments our relationship with our customers could lead to significant revenue reductions from these customers, impacting our revenue, cash flow, and liquidity.
- While we have not faced any adverse situation with our customers during the last three Fiscals, we cannot assure that we will not face any such situation in future.
- Furthermore, these key studios/ independent distributors/ customers might choose to switch to competitors or decline to renew or enter into new agreements on favourable terms.
- We cannot guarantee that we will maintain historical business levels with our key customers or significantly reduce our customer concentration, both of which could affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.
